## 2026-08-23 — `#24-abortrecoveryresiduals` (b): my own abort-swallowing debt cleared, 11 → 7, with a CONTROL ARM

The `#24-loopheadabort` fix made `_enter_warp_by_navigation` (and 16 other loops) able to raise
`StoryAbort`, which turned previously-unreachable `except BotModeError:` fallbacks into reachable
**abort swallowers**. This closes the debt that change created — and only that debt.

### ‼ THE ITEM SAID "FIVE SITES". RE-DERIVING FOUND 13 — AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS
A fresh AST pass (a broad handler whose TRY BODY can transitively reach `_check_abort`, and which
neither re-raises nor calls `reraise_if_aborting`) found **13 sites in 11 functions**, not 5. That is
not a contradiction — it is a WIDER criterion. Separating the two populations by re-running the same
analysis against `823cfa46`, the commit **before** the loop-head fix:
* **BEFORE: 7 swallowing functions.  AFTER the loop-head fix: 11.**
* ⇒ **4 functions (5 handler sites) are debt I CREATED** — `deliver_devon_goods_to_stern` (×2),
  `do_mauville_gym`, `get_rock_smash_hm`, `do_weather_institute`. These are exactly the five the
  adversarial review named; the re-derivation confirms it independently.
* ⇒ **7 functions are PRE-EXISTING** and are not mine. Filed as (c) rather than swept in silently.
‼ **A count is only comparable against the criterion that produced it.** Fixing "13" would have
misattributed 7 pre-existing defects to this change; fixing "5" without checking would have been
right by luck. The honest move was to compute both and say which is which.

### THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION
`except BotModeError:` → `except BotModeError as error:` + `reraise_if_aborting(error)` as the first
statement, at the five sites. ‼ **`reraise_if_aborting` is LATCH-KEYED**, so with no whiteout pending
it does nothing at all. Proven two-armed on the real function:
* **latch CLEAR (an ordinary nav failure): SWALLOWED → the fallback runs. Behaviour UNCHANGED.**
* **latch SET (a whiteout unwind): RE-RAISED.**
⇒ the only behaviour that changes is during a whiteout, which is precisely when it should.
‼ Worth naming why these needed fixing at all: all five were correct **BY ACCIDENT** — each
immediately calls `_navigate_riding_out`, whose own head check re-raises, so the abort escaped
incidentally. **Accidental correctness is what the KI-67/KI-81 family is made of.**

### ✅ RESULT, MEASURED
Swallowing functions **11 → 7**, and the 7 remaining are **byte-for-byte the pre-loop-head-fix set**
— i.e. my change now introduces **zero** abort-swallowing debt. Verified: `did I introduce any NEW
swallower? none`.

   this check reads only `CURRENT_STATE` files, and across ALL of them the phrase occurred exactly
   **ONCE** — my own sentence, written the same day. **Sixty lines of inference, three broken
   implementations and three review rounds existed to exempt a SINGLE SENTENCE**, which was then
   fixed by rewriting the sentence.
   ✅ The only exemption now is **`SUPERSEDE_RE`**, the retraction marker every sibling check in that
   file already honoured — and whose absence here was itself a review finding, so the check is now
   consistent with its neighbours instead of special.
   ⇒ **BEFORE BUILDING AN EXEMPTION, COUNT WHAT IT WOULD EXEMPT.** If the answer is "one", the
   exemption is the wrong tool.
   ⇒ **PREFER A DECLARED EXEMPTION OVER AN INFERRED ONE.** An inferred one is a guess about intent
   that stray punctuation can trigger; a declared marker IS the intent and cannot be faked.
   ⇒ And the rule that survives from the failed attempts: **run new tests against the OLD
   implementation — if they still pass, they do not discriminate and they prove nothing.** That is
   how v2 shipped: a rewrite that changed the SHAPE and not the TRUTH TABLE, with tests that agreed
   with it.
2. **(A) shipped with NO self-test.** Proven by three live arms, but the regression suite never
   exercised the branch — a later edit could delete it and `--self-test` would still print PASS.
   ✅ Added **F6/F7**. ‼ And documented the hazard at the mirror itself: `_decide()` duplicates the
   decision, so it can drift from the real function and keep passing. It covers the DECISION; only a
   LIVE arm covers the ATTRIBUTION, which is the half that actually broke. Keep both.
3. **(C) shipped with NO self-test** either. ✅ Added **C1–C5**, where C5 deliberately exercises the
   scanner's predicate on real files rather than only asserting set membership — a membership test
   alone would still pass if the scanning loop were deleted.
4. ⛔ **A "MEASURED" NUMBER THAT DESCRIBED THE WRONG THING.** I wrote *"0 hits across 631 .py files"*.
   The measurement was honest, but the gate's `_PY_ROOTS` scans the **whole fork trees**, not the
   `modules/` subdirectories I had counted: the real scope is **725** files (259 + 233 + 233), still
   0 hits. ⇒ **STATE THE SCOPE WITH THE COUNT.** A bare figure cannot be checked against the code it
   claims to describe, and "measured" is not a synonym for "correct".
5. A stale line-count figure in the handoff, re-derived and corrected.

‼ **AND AN OPERATIONAL INCIDENT WORTH RECORDING.** The reviewing agent, building a live fixture, hit
a silent `cd` failure and ran `git commit` against the REAL repository, creating an unauthorised
commit that swept up this item's in-review file. Nothing was lost or altered — only the commit
boundary moved, and it was never pushed. ⇒ **A SUBAGENT CAN WRITE TO YOUR TREE.** Give review agents
read-only instructions AND an explicit "do not run git write commands" line, and re-verify
`git status` after any review that built fixtures. (This is also why the standing rule is to stage
EXPLICIT PATHS: a blind `git add -A` in that state would have swept far more.)

### ⛔ ROUND 5 OF THE SAME ITEM: THE EQUALITY TEST WAS DIGIT-ONLY, AND A RULE FOR THAT ALREADY EXISTED

Closing the previous round's over-eager-guard finding, I required a FIGURE before the phrase so that
*"the ratchet fix was verified on BOTH forks"* would stop firing. That fixed the false positive and
opened a false-negative class: **`thirty-six on BOTH forks`, `the count is the same on BOTH forks`
and `identical on BOTH forks` all passed silently.**

‼ **THIS PROJECT HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THE PREVENTION RULE**, twice, in `08-MISTAKES.md`: *"A NUMERIC
GATE MUST ACCEPT THE FORMS HUMANS ACTUALLY WRITE — digits, spelled-out words… its silence means 'I
found no number in the form I know', which is NOT 'the number is right'"*, and *"when you gate a
FACT, gate the sentence as well as the number — ask 'can this claim be made without a digit?'"*.
I wrote a digit-only gate anyway. ⇒ **the recurring failure of this entire session: a rule filed
under one artifact does not fire while you are editing another.** It is exactly why these rules keep
being converted into gates and self-tests rather than left as prose.

✅ **FIXED: `_asserts_equality` now recognises three shapes** — a figure (`36`, `**36**`), a
spelled-out figure (`thirty-six`, word-bounded so `done`/`none` do not match `one`), or a sameness
word (`same|equal|identical|unchanged|alike|matches`). Windows are 14/24/40 chars respectively.
✅ **Both directions locked in:** R17–R20 assert each claim shape fires; R21/R22 assert an ACTION on
both forks (`verified`, `promoted`, `passes`) and the `done`/`none` word-boundary case stay quiet.
✅ **Fault-proven**: reverting `_asserts_equality` to digit-only fails R17, R18 and R19.
✅ **R23/R24 close the last gap the reviewer named** — the "forks forced EQUAL → silent" arm was true
but never locked into the suite. It now is, alongside R24 proving the same text fires again when the
baselines really differ. That pair is what makes this an INVARIANT test rather than a banned phrase.

### ⛔⛔ FINAL: THE RATCHET-CLAIM CHECK WAS DELETED, NOT FIXED — 289 LINES REMOVED

A six-angle adversarial review (false negatives / false positives / exemptions / test vacuity / docs
/ commit integrity, with a synthesizer that re-ran every claim) returned **7 blockers** on
`check_ratchet_baseline_claims`. All reproduced. The three that mattered:
* **it missed 7 of 7 genuine claims** — the figure had to be GLUED to the phrase, so a comma, a dash,
  an extra word, a table pipe or a newline defeated it. An end-to-end injection of seven
  present-tense equality claims into the live corpus produced **zero** findings.
* **it fired on innocent prose** — any nearby digit did it: dates, commit SHAs, line numbers, version
  strings. Following the gate's own remedy ("date-scope the sentence") *created* a violation.
* **its exemptions silenced ~5% of live lines** via markers that were not about the claim — a bypass
  this same file had already documented and fixed for a SIBLING check, which the new one did not
  inherit.

⇒ **The decisive question was not "can I fix those?" but "what does it protect?"** It reads only
CURRENT_STATE files, where the phrase appears a handful of times — all in prose ABOUT this check —
and the harm it prevents is a stale figure in a document that already tells readers to run the probe
instead. Six review rounds had gone into a documentation nicety.
✅ **DELETED**, with a long note at the former site so nobody rebuilds it. The stale-figure risk sits
where it always actually sat: the probe is the authority, KI-81's header carries the per-fork
figures, and reviewers catch drift — which is how all four original stale copies were found.

### ✅ AND THE CONTROL-CHARACTER GUARD'S OWN TEST WAS VACUOUS
The same review mutation-tested every self-test. `C5` re-implemented the predicate inline and **never
called `scan_py_ctrl_chars`** — so a mutant that gutted the scanner body, and one that deleted the
function and its wiring outright, BOTH passed with a green suite. My own comment beside it claimed
the opposite. ✅ Rewritten to call the shipped scanner against a fixture placed under `_PY_ROOTS`
(anywhere else and the scan skips it, which would be vacuous in a new way); both mutants now FAIL.
‼ **A test that does not call the thing it names is worse than no test**, because it also stops
anyone looking.

## 2026-08-23 — `#24-abortrecoveryresiduals` (c): the abort-swallow class is CLOSED in sandbox — 8 sites, 7 functions, ratchet 31 → 23

**This is bot behaviour, not tooling.** A whiteout raises `StoryAbort`, which is a `BotModeError`, so
every broad `except BotModeError:` in the story code can absorb the unwind and let the bot grind on
in a state it should have abandoned. `#24-abortswallow` fixed the first batch, `(b)` fixed the five
my own loop-head change had newly exposed, and **(c) closes the eight that predate all of it**.

`_talk_to_wandering_npc`, `sail_to_slateport`, `fight_route119_rival_and_get_fly`, `get_devon_scope`
(×2), `open_magma_hideout_entrance`, `do_magma_hideout`, `_aqua_challenge_matt`.

**THE FIX** is the same one-line, latch-keyed guard: `reraise_if_aborting(error)` as the handler's
first statement. Safe by construction — with no whiteout pending it does nothing at all.
✅ **Measured, not asserted.** An AST pass (handler whose try-body can transitively reach
`_check_abort`, neither re-raising nor calling `reraise_if_aborting`) went **8 sites / 7 functions →
ZERO**. Guarded handlers 14 → 22, exactly +8.
✅ **CONTROL-ARMED** as the probe's own message demands: with these guards removed it reads **31**,
with them present **23**. The drop is attributable to this change and nothing else. Baseline lowered
31 → 23. ⛔ **ON PROMOTION, LOWER custom 36 → 23 IN THE SAME COMMIT.**
✅ **BEHAVIOURAL TWO-ARM PROOF** on the exact handler shape now at all eight sites: latch CLEAR →
swallowed, old body runs (ordinary failures unchanged); latch SET → **re-raised**, the unwind escapes.

### TWO THINGS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE TOUCHING THESE HANDLERS AGAIN
* **Three of the eight are "accumulate into `tried`, then `continue`" search loops** — a deliberate
  try-every-neighbour pattern that is CORRECT for ordinary failures. They were not swallowing by
  sloppiness; they were DEFERRING a whiteout to "raise if all candidates fail", which is the wrong
  latency for an unwind. The guard changes only the abort case.
* **Five needed `as error` bound before the guard could be added, and that is not free.** Python
  UNBINDS an `except X as name:` target at handler exit — if the function already used a variable
  called `error`, binding it here would DELETE it. Checked all five by AST before editing; none did.

⚠ **Accepted semantic change, stated plainly:** while the latch is SET, an unrelated `BotModeError`
raised inside these handlers now also propagates rather than being handled locally. That is the
intended fail-safe direction — during a whiteout unwind the right move is to stop — and it matches
the 14 guards that already shipped.

⚠ Line insertions shifted three doc citations; the citation gate caught all three and they were
fixed by **re-parsing for the symbol**, not by offsetting the old numbers.

## 2026-08-23 — `#24-abortrecoveryresiduals` (a): ASSESSED, and the finding is THAT THE CODE WAS NOT CHANGED

The item asked for a reachability assessment before deciding urgency, and warned that shipping blind
into the whiteout-recovery path — this project's highest-risk area — is worse than a written-down
remote risk. The assessment says: **do not touch it.**

**What the failure requires.** The abort latch is set in exactly ONE place, `on_whiteout()`
(`story_mode.py:1246`), the framework's whiteout callback. `run()` CLEARS the latch at `:2606` and
then walks out of the Poké Center at `:2612-2627`. So the fatal path needs a SECOND genuine whiteout
landing inside that walk.

**Why that cannot realistically happen — measured, not argued:**
* **No battle can start there.** `gWildMonHeaders` parsed directly out of the ROM: Poké Center
  interiors carry no encounter header at all, and every respawn town has a land encounter rate of
  **0**. ‼ **RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY** with the project's OWN `get_wild_encounters_for_map`
  rather than a hand-rolled ROM parse, WITH POSITIVE CONTROLS to prove the reader works: **all 17
  towns/cities and all 32 Poké Center maps** read **0**; Routes 101/102 and Petalburg Woods read
  **12** (52 assertions, 0 BAD). *A reviewer caught the first version sampling 11 of 18 and 8 of 32
  while the prose said "every" — the committed script now proves the sentence it is cited for.* (The research agent reported 20 for those controls — a different counting, slots
  vs rate. ⇒ **the magnitude differs and the DISCRIMINATION does not**, which is the only thing
  the conclusion rests on. The figure recorded here is the one I measured.) Reproducible:
  `tools/story-dev/evidence/2026-08-23-abortrecovery-a-verify-landrate.py`.
* **`on_whiteout()` cannot fire twice on Emerald.** A single dispatch site (`_listeners.py:566`),
  gated behind `player_avatar_is_standing_still()`, which requires OVERWORLD — mutually exclusive
  with both live triggers. Corroborated empirically: **0 of 15,639 consecutive recovery pairs**
  lacked an intervening battle, i.e. not one spurious or duplicate recovery.
* **Never observed.** Across **16,688 recorded recoveries in 1,049 logs** — ‼ *those two counts I
  re-derived myself by grep, and they cross-check: 16,688 − 1,049 = 15,639, exactly the number of
  consecutive recovery PAIRS cited above* — the fatal signature appears **0 times**.
  ⚠ **NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED, and labelled so deliberately:** the finer frame statistics
  (min inter-whiteout gap 7,782 frames vs a median window of 1,525; 0 of 4,453 windows containing
  the next whiteout) come from the research agent's own parse, and neither I nor the reviewer
  reproduced the frame-window computation or committed the script that made it. They are
  SUPPORTING, not load-bearing — the conclusion rests on the land-encounter rate and the
  single-dispatch guarantee, both of which WERE independently verified.

‼ **And the window is NOT rare — it is entered 23-36 times in a normal run.** This is closed because
the SECOND whiteout is impossible there, NOT because recovery is uncommon. That distinction is the
whole assessment.

⚠ **RE-OPEN IF** the bot is run on **FireRed/LeafGreen** — a live duplicate-callback path exists
there (loop C can clear before `Task_RushInjuredPokemonToCenter` is created, re-arming the listener)
— or if respawn ever moves to a map with a non-zero land encounter rate.
⛔ The proposed fix stays recorded as correct-in-shape and UNPROVEN: `except StoryAbort: yield` ahead
of the `except BotModeError: raise` would make the whiteout branch match the DERAIL branch, which
already swallows-and-continues around the SAME `exit_building_after_whiteout()` call bounded by
`_derails > 4`. **Do not ship it without a driven double whiteout.**

### TWO GENUINELY NEW DEFECTS FELL OUT OF THE ASSESSMENT
* **`#24-pluginwhiteoutnoyield` (UPSTREAM).** `_listeners.py:567` calls `plugin_whiteout()` bare, with
  no `yield from`, and `plugin_whiteout` is a generator function — so the generator is created and
  discarded and **no plugin `on_whiteout()` hook has ever executed**. Verified independently, and
  present identically in the pristine mirror at `:536`, so it is upstream and must not be fixed
  there. Currently a no-op for us (no plugin implements the hook) — latent, not live.
* **`#24-harnesswhiteoutdrop`.** 36 real `Story -> Manual (whited out)` transitions, all in
  story-dev harness profiles and never in batch runs — harnesses pushing `run()` without setting
  `context.bot_mode_instance`, so the custom handling never engaged. A TEST-FIDELITY defect: any
  harness driver that whites out stops behaving like the real mode from that point on.

### AND A MEASURED TREND WORTH KEEPING
Max `WHITEOUT recovery #N` per x4 batch: **41 (the `recoveries > 40` ceiling) in nearly every batch
from 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-07, and never again after** (23-36 since). A wall at exactly the ceiling
value for a week and then never is the signature of a real behavioural fix; `SURVIVAL_WHITEOUT_
THRESHOLD = 3` is the obvious candidate and is live. ⛔ **Stated as CORRELATION WITH A DATE, NOT
ATTRIBUTION** — it is a max-across-lanes proxy over varying lane counts. Attributing it needs a
threshold-disabled A/B on one fixture, which nobody has run.

**The story frontier moved.** The Seafloor Cavern's nine rooms had been DRIVEN since 2026-08-14 but
were **not a chapter**: no module, nothing wired into `_play()`, and the drivers injected Dive with a

`modules/story/seafloor_cavern.py` (971 lines) — nine legs plus the orchestrator; wired as
**Segment 19b** (teach Dive organically) and **Segment 20** (the cavern), graded on
`_done_var("ROUTE128_STATE", 2)`.

### FOUR DRIVES OF THE PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT — not of a copy of it
| run | result |
|---|---|
| clean | `done=True var2=2 surfing=True at=(38,24) ocean_path=True` → **ACCEPTANCE: PASS** |
| fault: Room 8 push fails | **PASS**, `room8_recoveries=1` — the in-room jam recovery fired and the chapter still finished |
| fault: failure AFTER the Kyogre trigger | **PASS**, `route128_resumes=1` and **`room8_recoveries=0`** — attempt 2 never re-entered the cavern |

‼ **`room8_recoveries=0` in run 3 is the whole point.** It proves attempt 2 recognised that the
`(17,42)` trigger was disarmed PERMANENTLY and finished on Route 128 instead of re-diving ~25 minutes
into a guaranteed-fail arm check.
‼ **The acceptance includes "and the bot can continue"** — a real `calculate_path` from the launch
tile to the dive tile, proving the 1,766-tile OPEN OCEAN rather than the 41-tile closed lagoon.
§Ch15 ended four floors underground, §Ch18 on an eleven-tile island, §Ch19 in a living room, and ALL
THREE PASSED THEIR OWN TESTS.

### WHAT THE RESEARCH FOUND BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN
* **The decomp CORRECTED our own build spec.** It proposed a resume branch on *"the Kyogre flag is
  set but the var is < 2"*. That cannot discriminate: `setvar VAR_ROUTE128_STATE, 1` is at
  `Room9/scripts.inc:115`, **thirteen lines BEFORE** the flag at `:128`, in the same script — so no
  reachable state has the flag set and the var at 0. The shipped condition is `ROUTE128_STATE == 1`.
* **The grading name in every doc was wrong for our API.** `VAR_ROUTE128_STATE` is the decomp's
  spelling; `_event_vars` has the bare `ROUTE128_STATE`, and `get_event_var` returns **-1** for an
  unknown name. ⚠ Severity is lower than first claimed: `_done_var` RAISES on a phantom name, so
  only a raw `get_event_var` call fails silently.
* **Seven agents extracted the per-leg routing** rather than transcribing 800 lines of harness by
  eye. The seam walk (each leg's postcondition vs the next's precondition) found a missing constant
  and an inert recovery; the contradiction pass found the fabricated push table (below).

### ⛔ AND THE REVIEW FOUND FOUR BLOCKERS, ALL IN THE ORCHESTRATION GLUE — THE UNDRIVEN PART
1. **The Room 8 push loop had no per-push `try/except`,** so a jam propagated out and skipped the one
   fault-proven recovery entirely — turning a cheap in-room retry into a ~25-minute re-dive. The
   driven harness wraps EVERY push (`story_harness.py:8193-8200`); I transcribed only the happy path.
2. **The resume check ran once before the retry loop, not per attempt** — so one timeout after the
   trigger fired would burn attempts 2 and 3 on runs that could not possibly succeed.
3. **The anti-lagoon `calculate_path` was unguarded.** `PathFindingError` is a `RuntimeError`, not a
   `BotModeError`, so the assertion guarding the WORST outcome would have escaped the chapter's own
   retry handler as a raw traceback.
4. The outer retry loop was missing its loop-head `_check_abort()`.
⇒ **A DRIVEN HARNESS'S PER-STEP `try/except` AROUND A RETRIABLE ACTION IS PART OF THE PROVEN
BEHAVIOUR — TRANSCRIBE IT, NOT JUST THE STEPS.**

`repro_undefined_names.py` found **three undefined names** (`StoryAbort`, `reraise_if_aborting`,

during a push failure or a whiteout. They would have surfaced as a crash *during* recovery.

## 2026-08-27 — THE DAY'S THREE MEASURED MISTAKES ARE NOW GATES, NOT PROSE (`advise_on_diff.py` +3 rules)

The standing rule is *"anything enforceable belongs in a GATE, not in prose here — a rule already
broken is evidence that prose failed."* Today produced three mistakes whose shapes are mechanically
detectable in a diff, so they were written as `advise_on_diff.py` rules rather than as more text
nobody re-reads. All three are ADVISORY (the tool exits 0 either way and fires at `git commit` via
the fail-open PreToolUse hook), fault-tested BOTH ways, and — the part that matters — **verified
firing on this very day's real commit `a1b5e91b`**, i.e. they would have caught the three mistakes
as they were being made.

* **`R-WARPREST`** — fires on `warps_to` / `dest_warp` / `destination_location`. ⛔ A warp table
  gives the warp EVENT tile, not where the avatar RESTS: `(9,20)` targets `(31,16)` and the avatar
  rests on `(31,17)`; `1F (11,17)` targets `(9,5)` and rests on `(9,6)`; `B1F (9,3)` does not step
  at all. Per-warp, encoded nowhere. Tests T41/T42.
* **`R-SCANBOUND`** — fires on `for x/y in range(`. ⛔ Bound coordinate scans by the map's real
  `map_size`: tile lookup is a FLAT index, so an out-of-bounds x WRAPS and reports phantom
  coordinates (a 40×40 scan on a 19-wide map double-reported every warp). ‼ Carries the sharper
  half of the lesson too: a positive control proves a scan is not BLIND and says nothing about
  OVER-reporting — give such a control an expected COUNT, not just an expected member.
  Tests T43/T44.
* **`R-ACCEPTGRADE`** — fires on `ACCEPTANCE`. ⛔ A grade must enumerate the readings that actually
  happened, never count steps appended unconditionally; and it must include *"and the bot can
  CONTINUE"* — a real `calculate_path` off the END tile. ‼ And never walk to a DOOR tile to prove
  arrival: a path to a door ends INSIDE the building, which is how a driver skipped its whole
  end-matrix while printing PASS. Tests T45/T46.

`--self-test` now runs **40 checks** and enforces its own completeness: the T25 meta-check compares
the rule set against the registered positive-test set, and it **caught all three new rules shipping
untested** before they landed. `08-MISTAKES.md`'s three prevention rules now name their gate.

## 2026-08-27 — §Ch21 LEG 3 (SKY PILLAR), ATLAS PASS: OUR PLANNER IS READING A DIFFERENT SKY PILLAR THAN THE ATLAS MEASURED, AND IT ROUTES *THROUGH* 27 CRACKED TILES

The queue's instruction was **"DESIGN LEG 3 PROPER — THE SKY PILLAR, ATLAS FIRST, NOT A BUILD."**
This is that pass. Nothing was built; the design is deliberately **BLOCKED** on one measurement.

**NEW: `tools/story-dev/probe_ch21_skypillar.py`** — static, seconds, no network, two controls,
both fault-tested (`POKEBOT_SKYPILLAR_PROBE_FAULT=rig` makes the tile-blocking rig inert → C2 goes
RED, no measurements printed, exit 1). ‼ It is **not** a duplicate of
`probe_skypillar_clean_layout.py`: that decodes the DECOMP's `*_Clean` binaries over the network
and runs its own BFS; this asks the tile data and planner **our bot actually uses**. Keeping both
is the point — *they disagree*.

**⛔ THE FINDING.** Production reads **38 cracked tiles on 2F and 34 on 4F**; the atlas, reading
`*_Clean`, reports **0 and 5**. And because `map_path.py` has ZERO hits for `Cracked`, the planner
neither proposes the fall NOR avoids the cracks: **its own proposed climb crosses 27 of them** (13
on 2F, 14 on 4F). ⛔ `4F (11,1)->(5,4)` — which the atlas calls *"reachable without touching a
crack"* — crosses **14**. There is moreover **NO crack-free route across 2F or 4F at all** on the
layout we read. ⇒ **`navigate_to` IS UNSAFE ON 2F AND 4F.** `#24-crackedfloorpathfinder` is
sharpened accordingly: it is not merely that the planner "cannot express" the fall.

**⇒ THE CHAIN, WITH ITS ONE UNVERIFIED LINK NAMED.** The bot is **BIKELESS** here — MEASURED on
`post_wallace.ss1` (`RECEIVED_BIKE=False`, no bike among 26 bag slots, badges 1-7) — and cracked
floors are survived by SPEED. So a bikeless bot cannot cross 2F on the layout we read, yet the
story requires exactly that. **Therefore the story climb almost certainly runs on the CLEAN layouts
while our planner models the post-game ones.** ‼ The unverified link is *"a walking player falls"*,
which is the atlas's decomp claim and is **not** measured by this probe. It is printed in the
probe's own verdict rather than buried.

**✅ WHAT THE ATLAS GOT RIGHT, NOW CONFIRMED BY THE ORACLE RATHER THAN BY TWO BFS MODELS AGREEING:**
the route SHAPE. **Both sealed pockets REFUSE** (`3F (3,1)->(7,1)` and `4F (11,1)->(3,1)`), so the
deliberate fall is genuinely required; the post-fall walk `3F (6,4)->(7,1)` is **4 wp** and
`4F (7,1)->(3,1)` is **6 wp**. ⛔ Its STEP counts are not waypoint counts and were taken on the
other layout — 1F is **32 wp** not 17, 5F **43** not 34, TOP **13** not 14.

**✅ ONE REAL DE-RISKING:** floors **1F-5F carry ZERO object templates** (OUTSIDE has 1, TOP has 2),
so the loadedness false-block that sealed the Sootopolis pocket **cannot occur on the climb floors**.

**ALSO ADDED — `--driver ch21pocket` gains reading L5 (`CH21_LAYOUT_PROBE=1`)**: compares the LIVE
`gMapHeader` layout (`map.py:1750`) against the STATIC ROM header (`map.py:751`). Run on SOOTOPOLIS
at state 3 it returned **EQUAL — no runtime swap visible**. ⚠ Read narrowly: ONE map at ONE state.
The measurement that settles leg 3 is the same check run **on the Sky Pillar**, and that needs a
drive there. `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` returned to 3591/3600 by RETIRING the completed `#24-ch21anchor`
to a summary (its "verify an anchor with `probe_anchor_inventory.py`, never the driver's log"
lesson kept).

## 2026-08-27 — CORRECTION: DETAIL LOST WHEN `#24-ch21anchor` WAS RETIRED, RESTORED HERE (a Tier 1 review caught it)

⛔ **This is a repair, not new work.** Retiring `#24-ch21anchor` to a summary in `03-PUNCH-LIST.md`
(to keep that file under its 3600-line cap) left a pointer reading *"full detail in
`07-CHANGELOG.md`"* — **and that promise was false.** An independent Tier 1 review grepped the whole
`PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/` tree and found two load-bearing facts had vanished from the summary, from the
changelog entry it pointed at, and from everywhere else. The standing rule is *"retire by SUMMARISE
+ POINT, never delete — do not delete hard-won detail."* I deleted. Restoring verbatim:

* **WHY THE ANCHOR WAS NEEDED AT ALL.** `probe_anchor_inventory.py` over all **77** saves: the
  frontier stopped at `post_dive.ss1` / `post_space_center.ss1` — **nothing existed after the
  Seafloor Cavern.** Until one was captured, *every* §Ch21 measurement paid a full §Ch20 drive
  (~25 min) before it could start, "which is precisely the cost that makes people skip the
  measurement."
* **⛔ WHY `--driver anchorcapture` COULD NOT BE USED.** It navigates to a map/tile, and **ROUTE128
  is visited BOTH before and after the cavern**, so a map-only target cannot tell the two eras
  apart. **The discriminator must be `ROUTE128_STATE == 2`.** ‼ This is the general lesson, and it
  outlives the item: *an anchor's identity is the VAR that gates its era, never the map you are
  standing on* — the same rule playbook §0b Q3 states as "name the flag/var that gates the content
  and assert it on the anchor."

‼ **THE PROCESS LESSON, which is the reason this entry exists rather than a silent re-edit.** A
retirement is a MOVE, and a move is only complete when the destination is verified to contain the
content. I wrote the pointer and did not read the destination. ⇒ **When retiring an item, grep the
destination for the specific facts you are dropping, before you drop them** — "full detail in X" is
a claim about X, and it is exactly as checkable as any other claim in this tree.

## 2026-08-27 — §Ch21 SKY PILLAR RECON: THE LAYOUT QUESTION IS SETTLED, AND FIVE DRIVE-KILLERS ARE NAMED — INCLUDING A SECOND DELIBERATE FALL THE ATLAS NEVER CONTAINED

Seven read-only agents on separate angles (our ROM reader, the decomp, the fall mechanic, the exit
route, the layout swap, an adversarial refutation, and fixture/cost). ⚠ **Its verification pass did
NOT run** — both adjudicating critics died on an account session limit. Per the standing rule this
section is therefore a **NOTE, not truth**; claims marked MEASURED carry a decomp quote or our own
probe output, the rest are inferences. ⛔ Re-run the critics before any of it becomes code.

**✅ THE QUESTION THAT BLOCKED THE BUILD IS ANSWERED.** Six Sky Pillar maps (1F-5F, TOP) swap to
`LAYOUT_SKY_PILLAR_*_CLEAN` via `setmaplayoutindex` in each floor's `OnTransition`, gated
`call_if_lt VAR_SKY_PILLAR_STATE, 2`. **The story climb runs entirely on CLEAN** (the var is 0 for
the whole ascent). `setmaplayoutindex` writes only `gSaveBlock1Ptr->mapLayoutId` and the live
`gMapHeader` — never the compiled `gMapGroups` table our reader uses ⇒ **our planner reads the
post-game layout, confirmed.** `SKY_PILLAR_ENTRANCE` and `SKY_PILLAR_OUTSIDE` do **not** swap at all.

**⛔⛔ THE FINDING THAT WOULD HAVE COST THE MOST: THE DESCENT NEEDS A *SECOND* DELIBERATE FALL.**
Coming down, `Top -> 5F -> 4F (3,1)` lands in 4F's **12-tile WEST POCKET**, which has no walking
exit. Without a second fall through `4F (0,3)`/`(1,3)` the bot summits, **wakes Rayquaza** (flipping
the layouts DIRTY for every subsequent load) and is **STRANDED** — the §Ch15/§Ch18/§Ch19
"passed its own test while stranded" shape, and the atlas contained no hint of it.

**⛔ FOUR MORE THAT BREAK A FIRST DRIVE:** four Sky Pillar warps are **ARROW WARPS that do not fire
on step** (`Entrance (6,16)`/`(14,4)`, `1F (6,13)`/`(7,13)`) — a walk-only planner stalls forever
with no error; `SkyPillar_Outside`'s `ON_FRAME` Wallace cutscene fires on **map load** at
`SOOTOPOLIS_CITY_STATE == 3` with no coord condition and **drives the player 12 tiles under
`lockall`**; `ROUTE131` swaps its layout **UNCONDITIONALLY** (116 static-open tiles are live walls);
and `SKY_PILLAR_TOP` **inverts** the layout subset (31 static-open tiles are CLEAN walls).

**‼ TWO AGENTS CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER ON A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM, AND THE CRITICS WERE NOT THERE TO
ADJUDICATE.** One argued the stale model "can never route the bot onto a real CLEAN crack"; the
other showed the same arithmetic means a crack-avoiding route costs **exactly the same** (29 vs 29;
6 vs 6; TOP 13 vs 13) ⇒ **which route A* returns is a pure TIE-BREAK.** The conservative reading
wins: the planner **may** cross a real crack, and if the tie-break picks **(9,4)** the bot falls into
3F's MAIN region — the documented decoy — wasting the climb. ⇒ **the build must BAN 4F's five
CLEAN-cracked tiles explicitly**; equal cost makes that free. ⛔ The first version of this changelog
and the atlas carried the *stronger, wrong* claim for about twenty minutes; it is corrected in place.

**✅ AND ONE OF THE DAY'S OWN FINDINGS WAS UPGRADED.** The warp resting-tile offset is **not**
per-warp magic — `SetUpWarpExitTask()` branches on the metatile behaviour **at the warp target
tile**: the `MB_NON_ANIMATED_DOOR` (0x60) family exits one tile SOUTH. Blind-tested **3/3** against
the day's live readings *including the discriminating negative* (`B1F (9,3) -> 1F (14,5)`, not a
door, rests exactly). ⇒ all eight Sky Pillar staircases rest one tile south of their table target.
`advise_on_diff.py`'s `R-WARPREST` was refined accordingly: read the target tile's behaviour first
(free), treat a drive as CONFIRMATION — but still never grade against the raw warp target.

**GAP CLOSED:** `3F_Clean (3,1) -> (11,1)` — the leg the atlas's route depends on — had **never**
been measured by any committed tool. It is **28 moves** on CLEAN; 3F's main region from (3,1) is 118
tiles, contains (11,1) and does NOT contain (7,1), independently re-confirming the sealed pocket.
